key_insight: Estimating any valid transport map is fundamentally limited by minimax sample complexity, and under common OT stability assumptions it is statistically as hard as estimating the optimal transport map itself.
engineering_relevance: For generative modeling systems using diffusion, flow matching, or normalizing flows, this means choosing an easier-to-train transport target may not reduce the underlying statistical difficulty unless OT stability assumptions fail.
method: Formulates valid transport-map estimation in a minimax framework.
Derives sample-complexity lower bounds for transport maps/plans used by modern generative methods.
Shows that when OT stability assumptions break, non-OT transport maps can be learned more accurately than the OT map.
evidence_signal: The paper is a theoretical analysis based on minimax lower bounds and illustrative examples, rather than empirical benchmarking on a dataset.
watch_item: The strongest hardness result relies on stability assumptions from optimal transport theory, which may not hold in all practical data-generating settings.
paper_title: The Fundamental Limits of Valid Transport Map Estimation
